goal: Lets multiple local CI container runs happen at once by giving each job its own isolated Docker network instead of a shared one with fixed IPs.
Fixes a side effect from an earlier CI change (#33362) that currently blocks concurrent local CI runs.

result.summary: This PR isolates Docker networks used by local CI container runs, naming each network per-container and deriving a unique subnet from a hash of the container name, so two CI jobs can run concurrently without IP collisions. It also adds cleanup of these networks on successful runs, and threads the routable test IPs through environment variables instead of hardcoding them in two functional tests. The change is a follow-up fix for a regression introduced by an earlier CI PR (#33362).
result.problem: Local CI jobs currently share fixed Docker networks with static routable IPs, so a second concurrent CI run cannot start because it can't claim the same static addresses; this blocks contributors from running CI locally in parallel.

resolved_concerns: maflcko's nits about combining the two subnets into one network call, assigning both IPs together, and simplifying a verbose hunk were all addressed by the author in a follow-up push and the author replied 'done'/'neat' to each.
maflcko also suggested renaming the env var prefix so it isn't tied to CI; author applied the suggested diff.
